Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our compliance team needs formal evidence to close the vendor acceptance checklist for the on-prem/private VPC deployment. Specifically we need:

- Final control/data-plane boundary diagram (annotated with IP ranges and NAT egress points)
- Runbook excerpt showing canary cutover steps and rollback triggers
- Evidence of egress proofing (what traffic is allowed, proxy behavior, and test plan)
- Confirmation of KMS/HSM integration for tenant keys and key rotation cadence

Can you share the artifacts and a short note (1-2 paragraphs) confirming the acceptance criteria are met?

I've attached our vendor checklist (Stratus-Vendor-Checklist.pdf) — see highlighted items 4, 7, and 11. We aim to complete this by end of week so the operations team can schedule the cutover.

Thanks,
Ashley

Hi Ashley —

Appreciate the checklist and the clear callouts. Attached are the artifacts requested; high-level notes below.

Attachments included: redwood-private-vpc-schematic-v3.pdf, egress-proofing-checklist.xlsx

Quick summary (acceptance highlights):
- Control plane endpoints are colocated in the management VPC with dedicated peering to the tenant data plane; diagram annotates public vs private endpoints and IP CIDR ranges.
- Data plane pods run in tenant VPC subnets with egress NAT through audited proxies in the perimeter cluster (see egress checklist tab).
- Canary cutover runbook excerpt: 1) route canary tenant traffic to dedicated pool, 2) observe latency/error metrics for 2 hours, 3) expand to 50% for 4 hours, 4) full cutover on green — rollback triggers enumerated in step 5.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed keys via the agreed KMS integration (rotate keys every 90 days by policy; documented rotation playbook attached).

Next steps:
- Please confirm the highlighted vendor checklist items are satisfied or list any remaining gaps.
- If acceptable, we propose a cutover window for Tue 2026-11-30 02:00-06:00 UTC (low-traffic).

CC'ing Karthik and Mina for any technical clarifications.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Sat, Nov 21, 2026 at 14:05 Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attached are the artifacts requested; high-level notes below.

Adding a few technical clarifications to make the operational acceptance crisp:

- Ports & protocols: control plane uses mTLS over TCP 8443 for control RPCs; data plane north-south uses TCP 443 terminated at the egress proxy. All inter-pod traffic remains within the tenant subnets (no cross-tenant routing).
- NAT pattern: 1:many NAT with ephemeral source port mapping sitting in the perimeter proxy cluster; egress IPs are listed in the schematic under "Perimeter NAT Pool" (10.240.128.0/27).
- Health checks & canary metrics: we recommend the acceptance include at least 2 full rolling windows of the 99th percentile tail latency and a failure-rate threshold <0.5% during canary. We note these in the runbook excerpt (section 3).
- Audit evidence: we've exported a short set of test flows (pcap + aggregated logs) showing only approved destinations during the egress test — linking the Jira ticket for retrieval.

I've pushed a small amendment to the schematic (v3.1) in the Drive link; the key change documents the management plane's ephemeral egress for telemetry (separate from tenant egress).

Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2987

If Stratus wants, we can perform an on-call walkthrough of the runbook and execute the test steps together in a short session (30–45m).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — team read through the schematic and runbook excerpt. Two quick items before we mark the vendor checklist closed:

2) Please confirm the agreed cutover slot (Tue 2026-11-30 02:00-06:00 UTC) and share the cutover checklist with owner names for each step.

Everything else looks good; the KMS rotation cadence and control/data separation notes satisfy our security group. If you can drop the logs and the step-owner checklist by COB Monday (2026-11-29), we'll finalize and schedule the cutover.

Happy to do a joint run-through on Mon if you'd prefer.
